input_state.terrain: US controls all bulk landing/logistics nodes and the great majority of useful maneuver terrain; several eastern/northern and bombproof strongpoints remain coherent.

US_adaptation.method: Continue tank-engineer-75mm reduction teams with observed destroyer/CVE fires; avoid unsupported infantry rushes. Damage assessment remains imperfect and some supposedly neutralized positions reopen locally.
US_adaptation.Makin_release: Makin organized resistance ended 27 Nov afternoon. Three-CVE-class support is not teleported; one deck-equivalent remains tied to Makin/transport-ASW reorganization through much of the morning while roughly two deck-equivalents become available to reinforce Tarawa support from late morning through afternoon.
US_adaptation.naval_fire: Close destroyer/cruiser fires remain available, but seaward pickets stay reinforced after the 26/27 Type-93 raid; not every destroyer can be simultaneously used as a shore-fire platform.

timeline.event: Japanese pockets conduct small infiltration, sniper and local grenade/mortar actions only; no coherent mass counterattack can be generated. US holds reduction positions and prepares registered fires.

US armor-engineer teams reduce several reopened/previously bypassed strongpoints. Japanese local wire/ammunition separation keeps individual positions active longer than US damage reports initially assume.
First meaningful Makin-released CVE support begins augmenting Tarawa CAS/spotting/ASW. This increases tempo but does not instantly erase hardpoints.
Eastern/northern coherent pockets are compressed and split. Japanese local C2 ceases to function beyond small strongpoint groups; ammunition and water shortage become decisive in several positions.
Last mutually supporting strongpoint clusters are isolated. Centered coherent organized resistance collapses around 21:30-23:30; several bombproof/isolated groups continue firing into the night.

losses_11_28.note: Japanese loss band includes locally armed support caught in final reductions; it is not a claim that all remaining support personnel were first-line infantry.

T24_state.territory: US controls essentially all operationally useful Betio terrain; remaining Japanese action is isolated strongpoint/straggler resistance rather than a mutually supporting island defense system.
T24_state.secure_declaration: NOT_YET at 11/28T24. Centered formal secure declaration after dawn sweep on 29 Nov.

guards: No historical 20-Nov reef catastrophe is restored; 24-Nov tide/lane advantages remain paid.
No post-GALVANIC cave/defense doctrine is retrojected into Betio.
No mission-capable Japanese tank is restored after the 27-Nov closeout.
US adaptation is competent but not omniscient; reopened positions and false suppression assessments remain possible.
